title: Check that a bar chart starts at zero
description: Look at a bar chart and say whether the value axis starts at zero. If it does not, the bar lengths are not a fair comparison.
oneStarDescription: Point to the axis that carries the numbers.
twoStarDescription: Read the first number. Say whether it is zero.
threeStarDescription: If it is not zero, say the longest bar may look more different than the numbers are.

title: Check a caller using a number you already trust
description: If a call or message claims to be your bank or another official body, contact them on a number from their site or a statement, not from the message.
oneStarDescription: End the call or close the message without giving a detail.
twoStarDescription: Use the number on your card, a paper statement, or the organisation's own website.
threeStarDescription: Call that number and ask whether they were trying to reach you.

title: Choose hatching or crosshatching for one shadow
description: Look at one shadow and say whether separate lines or crossed lines will darken it, then do only that.
oneStarDescription: Point to one shadow on the object or the sculpture.
twoStarDescription: Say hatching if a single direction is enough, or crosshatching if you need it darker.
threeStarDescription: Make the mark you named and do not add the other in that patch.

title: Choose the right place to report a scam
description: A suspicious email goes to the NCSC. Money already lost, in England, Wales, or Northern Ireland, goes to Report Fraud or the bank.
oneStarDescription: Say whether you only received a message, or whether money or an account has already gone.
twoStarDescription: If it is only a suspicious email, use report@phishing.gov.uk. If money is gone, contact the bank and Report Fraud.
threeStarDescription: Do not send a fraud report only to the phishing address.

title: Clean a toileting accident without punishing the cat
description: Wash the spot and do not punish the cat. If accidents are regular, the next step is a vet, not a punishment.
oneStarDescription: When you find the accident, do not shout or push the cat toward it.
twoStarDescription: Wash the area with a biological or enzymatic wash made for this, and let it dry.
threeStarDescription: If this keeps happening, write that you will ask a vet, and stop there.

title: Compare an HB mark with a 6B mark
description: Make one patch with an HB pencil and one with a 6B, and say which is darker and which is harder.
oneStarDescription: If you have both grades, write HB and 6B beside two boxes. If you have only one, say so and stop.
twoStarDescription: Fill each box with that pencil, using a similar pressure.
threeStarDescription: Say which patch is darker and which point feels harder.

title: Crosshatch a form and lift one highlight
description: Lay a second set of lines across the first so a round form darkens, then erase one highlight.
oneStarDescription: Draw a second set of lines across the hatch, on the darker side.
twoStarDescription: Let the direction of the lines turn with the object, as around a round fruit.
threeStarDescription: Erase a small patch where the light hits, and leave the rest.

title: Describe where you live in a few simple sentences
description: Say a few simple sentences about where you live: the place, and one thing around it.
oneStarDescription: Say the town or the kind of home.
twoStarDescription: Add one concrete detail, such as a shop, a station, or a garden.
threeStarDescription: Join the two sentences with a simple and or but, and stop.

title: Draw a blind contour while looking at the object
description: Look at the object, not the paper, and let the pencil follow the edge.
oneStarDescription: Set your eyes on the object or a sculpture you may study.
twoStarDescription: Move the pencil as your eye moves along one edge, without checking the page.
threeStarDescription: Look at the drawing only after the line is done, and name one proportion that went astray.

title: Draw a contour without redrawing the line
description: Draw the outline in one continuous line and do not go back over it.
oneStarDescription: Put the pencil where the outline begins and keep moving.
twoStarDescription: When you are tempted to darken a bit, leave that bit as one line.
threeStarDescription: Show an outline that is one pass, not a fuzzy bundle of repeats.

title: End an exchange when you cannot continue it
description: Manage a very short exchange, and stop when you can no longer keep it going.
oneStarDescription: Ask or answer one routine question.
twoStarDescription: Give one more simple fact, such as a time or a place.
threeStarDescription: When you cannot go on, say so, in either language, and stop.

title: Find a familiar word on a simple notice
description: On a notice, menu, or poster, point to one familiar word or name and say what you think it refers to.
oneStarDescription: Use a notice or menu you may read.
twoStarDescription: Point to a word you recognise.
threeStarDescription: Say what that word tells you, and name one part you are not claiming to understand.

title: Find one predictable fact in a menu or a timetable
description: Find one price, time, or place in a simple menu or timetable, and point to it.
oneStarDescription: Say which fact you are looking for, such as a price or a departure.
twoStarDescription: Point to the line that has it.
threeStarDescription: Read that fact aloud and leave the rest of the page.

title: Follow one slow instruction in the language you are learning
description: Follow one concrete instruction said slowly, and ask for a repeat if you need it.
oneStarDescription: Have someone say one short instruction, slowly.
twoStarDescription: Do the action if you understood it.
threeStarDescription: If you did not, ask them to say it again, and do it only then.

title: Forward a suspicious email without clicking
description: Forward the email to report@phishing.gov.uk and do not open its links. Junk you already left in spam need not be forwarded.
oneStarDescription: Leave every link and attachment closed.
twoStarDescription: Forward the message to report@phishing.gov.uk.
threeStarDescription: If a one-link email is rejected as already-known spam, do not keep resending it.

title: Gesture-draw an object in one minute
description: Keep the pencil on the paper and use longer strokes, not circles, to catch the whole shape in under a minute.
oneStarDescription: Put the pencil on the paper and do not lift it for the first pass.
twoStarDescription: Follow the long directions of the object rather than circling in place.
threeStarDescription: Stop when a minute has passed and show the sheet.

title: Give each cat a hide of their own
description: In a home with more than one cat, each cat has a place to get out of sight.
oneStarDescription: Count the enclosed rests and the cats.
twoStarDescription: Add a box or bed with a way in until there is at least one per cat.
threeStarDescription: Move one hide off the main path so a cat can leave the others.

title: Hand over the list of pieces you will play
description: Write the titles you will perform, with the composer, and give that list to the listener before you start.
oneStarDescription: Write each piece and the composer.
twoStarDescription: Number them in the order you will play.
threeStarDescription: Give the paper to the listener before the first note.

title: Hatch a shadow with lines that do not cross
description: Fill a shadow with separate parallel lines. Closer lines make it darker. They do not cross.
oneStarDescription: Make a simple outline of the object.
twoStarDescription: Fill the shadow with lines that stay apart and share one direction.
threeStarDescription: Make one area darker by placing lines closer, not by crossing them.

title: Introduce yourself and someone with you
description: In a language you are learning, say who you are and who is with you, using phrases you can actually say.
oneStarDescription: Say your name and one phrase for hello.
twoStarDescription: Say the other person's name as they have agreed you may say it.
threeStarDescription: If you lose the phrase, ask the other speaker to slow down, and stop.

title: Leave a QR code in an email unscanned
description: A QR code in an email is a link. Do not scan it. A code on a menu in front of you is a different situation.
oneStarDescription: Point to the QR code in the message and do not open the camera on it.
twoStarDescription: Say that this code is inside a message you did not trust, so you will not scan it.
threeStarDescription: If you still need the organisation, go to the site you already know, not through the code.

title: Leave enough litter to dig and cover
description: Put in a layer the cat can dig and use to cover, rather than a thin scatter.
oneStarDescription: Look at the tray and say whether a paw could dig.
twoStarDescription: Add litter until the layer is deep enough to cover waste, without filling the tray to the rim.
threeStarDescription: If you can do so without disturbing the cat, see whether they can turn and cover.

title: Leave the carrier out as an ordinary bed
description: Leave the carrier in a place the cat already likes, with something that smells of home inside it.
oneStarDescription: Leave the carrier open where the cat already sits, not only on travel days.
twoStarDescription: Put a piece of their bedding inside and leave the door open.
threeStarDescription: If the cat steps in, give a treat and stop. Do not push them in.

title: Use a short look before you sight-read
description: When you are given unseen music, use a short preparation to look and try any part. The performance starts after that.
oneStarDescription: Look at the page. You may play or sing any bar during this look.
twoStarDescription: Point to one rhythm or leap you will be careful with.
threeStarDescription: Start the piece only after that look, and keep going to the end of the short test.

title: Match bars or columns to the comparison
description: Use bars for categories. For time, use columns. Say so before you draw three values.
oneStarDescription: Say whether you are comparing categories or moments in time.
twoStarDescription: Choose horizontal bars for categories, or vertical columns for time.
threeStarDescription: Draw three bars or columns from zero and label them.

title: Name the pressure in a suspicious message
description: Before you click, name which pressure the message uses: authority, urgency, emotion, scarcity, or a news hook.
oneStarDescription: Do not tap the link. Put the phone or the mouse down.
twoStarDescription: Say which of those five signs you can see, or say you cannot see one.
threeStarDescription: Leave the link and the attachment untouched.

title: Offer a high rest a cat can get onto safely
description: Give a raised place large enough to lie on, that the cat can reach and leave without a fall.
oneStarDescription: Pick a shelf, a wardrobe top, or a cat tree the cat can reach.
twoStarDescription: Put a steady step or choose a height the cat already uses, and move breakable things off the edge.
threeStarDescription: See the cat go up and down once, and take the rest away if it wobbles.

title: Order category bars from largest to smallest
description: When the categories have no other order, sort the bars from the largest value to the smallest.
oneStarDescription: Write three categories and the numbers you counted or were given.
twoStarDescription: Put the largest value first and the smallest last.
threeStarDescription: Draw the bars in that order, with the axis starting at zero.

title: Place a litter tray away from food and sleep
description: Put the tray in a quiet place, not beside the food, water, or bed.
oneStarDescription: Choose a spot that is not a busy corridor or a noisy room, and put the empty tray there.
twoStarDescription: Move the food and water so they are not next to the tray, and keep the bed elsewhere.
threeStarDescription: Once the cat uses it, do not stand over them or move the tray mid-use.

title: Provide one tray per cat and a spare
description: Count the cats and set out one tray each, plus one extra.
oneStarDescription: Count the cats who share the home.
twoStarDescription: Put down one more tray than that count, in more than one quiet place if you can.
threeStarDescription: Look at each tray and say whether a cat can step in and turn.

title: Read one bar as a length from zero
description: Read one bar by its length from zero, and say the value the gridline or the label gives.
oneStarDescription: Point to one bar and name its category.
twoStarDescription: Read the number at its end, using the axis.
threeStarDescription: Say whether it is longer or shorter than one other bar, and stop.

title: Replace the litter on a weekly rhythm
description: Spot-clean the tray each day you use it, and replace the litter at least once in the week.
oneStarDescription: Remove the soiled clumps today and leave enough litter for the cat to dig.
twoStarDescription: Write the day you will empty and replace the litter, within seven days of the last full change.
threeStarDescription: Empty the tray on that day, wash it with a product that is safe for cats, and put fresh litter back.

title: Review one public detail a scam could copy
description: Look at one thing your profile shows and decide whether a stranger needs to see it.
oneStarDescription: Open a social profile you control.
twoStarDescription: Point to one detail, such as a birthday, a pet's name, or a workplace.
threeStarDescription: Hide it or leave it, and say which you chose.

title: Roll a moist soil sample into a ball
description: Wet about a spoonful until crumbs break down, then see whether it will form a ball.
oneStarDescription: Add water a little at a time and knead until crumbs break.
twoStarDescription: Press it into a ball. If it falls apart, say so.
threeStarDescription: Say only whether it held a ball. Do not announce a percentage of clay.

title: Take a soil sample from below the surface
description: Take the pinch from about 15 centimetres down, not from the loose surface, then put the hole back.
oneStarDescription: Move leaves aside and dig a small hole about a hand's depth.
twoStarDescription: Take a small sample from that depth and put it in a clean container.
threeStarDescription: Put the soil back and wash your hands.

title: Scribble outward from the middle of an object
description: Start in the middle of something you can see and scribble outward until the overall shape appears. Finish in under two minutes.
oneStarDescription: Put one object where you can see it, and start the pencil in the middle of the page.
twoStarDescription: Use circular marks that grow outward until the outer shape is there.
threeStarDescription: Stop before two minutes and leave the scribble, even if details are missing.

title: Set out play for an indoor cat
description: An indoor cat needs more to do. Put out a toy and a space to climb, then play and stop.
oneStarDescription: Clear a short path the cat can run without meeting a hazard.
twoStarDescription: Bring out one toy and play until the cat loses interest.
threeStarDescription: End the game and leave a scratching post or a climb still available.

title: Settle a cat indoors after a move
description: Keep the cat inside after a house move, then use short supervised trips outside before any free roaming.
oneStarDescription: For the first fortnight, keep the cat indoors and show them the tray, water, and a hide.
twoStarDescription: When their behaviour has settled, go out with them for a short time, not at dawn or dusk.
threeStarDescription: Call them back with food, and end the outing while they are still near you.

title: Shade by changing pencil pressure
description: On a second gesture drawing, press lightly on the lit side and harder where the shadow is.
oneStarDescription: Point to the bright side and the dark side of the object.
twoStarDescription: Use a light pressure on the bright side and a heavier pressure in the shadow.
threeStarDescription: Show one place where the tone changes gradually, not as a hard stripe.

title: Stipple a tone with dots
description: Build a dark patch from dots, and keep the dots from turning into lines.
oneStarDescription: Place dots far apart on the lighter side.
twoStarDescription: Place dots closer where the object is darker.
threeStarDescription: Look for a place where dots joined into a line, and stop or separate them.
